chamfer_distance — 3D metrics op

• Data kinds: points × points → measurement

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.chamfer_distance(a, b, squared=False) (to call the implementation directly, import metrics3d; metrics3d.chamfer_distance(a, b, squared=False); from the registry, ops3d.get("chamfer_distance"))

Usage

The symmetric Chamfer distance = 0.5*(mean_a min_b + mean_b min_a). → scalar. Smaller is a closer match.

Raises ValueError: if either is empty or not (N,3) (the mean of an empty set = a silent NaN).

Computation: with scipy.spatial.cKDTree, take the nearest-neighbour distance d_ab from each point of a to b ((Na,)) and d_ba from b to a, then 0.5 * (mean(d_ab) + mean(d_ba)). With squared=True each distance is raised to the power 2 before averaging (the unit becomes distance^2; the form used in gradient-based optimisation). The default is the raw distance (unit = the coordinate unit).

Input: a, b are point clouds (N, 3) / (M, 3) (point counts may differ, no correspondence needed). Converted to float. Align the coordinate frame and scale of the two beforehand (comparing 2 clouds before registration merely measures the pose difference).

Returns: Python float. 0 for identical point clouds. Range [0, inf), not normalised (it scales with the cloud size, so divide by e.g. the bbox diagonal when comparing).

Note: being a mean, it is less affected by outliers than Hausdorff, but it is sensitive to uneven point density (the mean of the denser side dominates). To equalise density, apply pc_poisson_disk / voxel_grid_downsample first. For threshold-based evaluation use fscore, for the worst case hausdorff_distance, and with known correspondence rmse_correspondence.
